lead.t: The sigmoid colon is a common site, although caecal volvulus also occurs.

b: Much less common than sigmoid volvulus (about one-third of colonic volvulus compared with about 65% for the sigmoid), with a mortality of up to 20% .

Caused by a mobile caecum sharing a common mesentery with the terminal ileum (failure of fixation), which rotates (usually clockwise ) out of the right iliac fossa towards the mid or left upper abdomen , producing a closed loop obstruction
Peak age 30 to 40 years , commoner in women . A trigger is often recent surgery (laparotomy, gynaecological procedures), pregnancy, a high-fibre diet, or an obstructing colonic cancer.

Presentation: non-specific abdominal pain (almost invariable) with nausea, vomiting, constipation and distension in about a third. In thin patients one may palpate a resonant, distended caecum in the centre or upper abdomen with an empty ri

X-ray: a gas-filled, comma-shaped or "coffee bean" caecum pointing to the left upper quadrant , with small bowel obstruction and a collapsed distal colon. CT shows the whirl sign. A contrast enema can show a "beak" at the twist.
